title: Hepatitis C PCR (viral load)
what: This blood test looks for the hepatitis C virus itself and shows how much of it is in your blood.
why: If hepatitis C antibodies were found, to see whether the virus is there now. Also before, during, and after treatment.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: If you were treated for hepatitis C, and when it ended
If you have other liver conditions or HIV

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast strictly, but it is better to come 3 to 4 hours after a light, non-fatty meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: If you are on treatment, keep taking it as scheduled. Do not skip pills before the test.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A sleeve you can easily roll up above the elbow.

bring: Your referral or list of tests
Your treatment summary, if you had treatment
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow, and you are asked to clench your fist a few times
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick. Blood fills the tubes in a few seconds
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Until you get the result, use only your own razor and toothbrush
Your result is confidential. Only you or your doctor will get it.
red_flags: The puncture site is very swollen, painful, and red

faq.q: I have antibodies but no virus. What does that mean?
faq.a: Often it means you met the virus at some point, but it is not there now. Your doctor will tell you for sure.
Yes. Today it is usually cured with tablets. Your doctor will choose the treatment.

reminders.text: Hepatitis C PCR tomorrow. Better to skip fatty food in the morning. Take medicines as usual.
